text: Which dinosaur had three horns and a large bony frill?
explanation: Triceratops had two long horns above its eyes, a shorter nose horn, and a bony frill behind its head.
hint: Look for a dinosaur with a special head shape.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: What kind of food did Tyrannosaurus rex eat?
explanation: Tyrannosaurus rex was a carnivore: a meat-eating dinosaur. Its powerful jaws and sharp teeth were suited to eating other animals.
hint: Think about what sharp teeth can help an animal eat.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which dinosaur had large plates along its back?
explanation: Stegosaurus had two rows of bony plates along its back and spikes on its tail. Scientists still study what the plates were used for.
hint: Think about the shapes along the dinosaur’s back.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which of these dinosaurs had a very long neck?
explanation: Brachiosaurus was a long-necked, plant-eating dinosaur. Its front legs were longer than its back legs, giving its body a sloping shape.
hint: Compare the body shapes of these dinosaurs.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which dinosaur had a heavy bony club at the end of its tail?
explanation: Ankylosaurus had armour on its body and a bony tail club. The club could be used for defence.
hint: Look for a dinosaur with body armour.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

explanation: Diplodocus was a herbivore, which means a plant eater. It had a long neck, a long tail, and peg-like teeth.
hint: Its teeth helped it gather food, rather than tear meat.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which dinosaur had tall back spines that formed a sail-like shape?
explanation: Spinosaurus had tall spines on its back that formed a sail-like shape. Scientists are still investigating how it used this feature.
hint: Think about a dinosaur with an unusual outline.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which dinosaur had a pointed spike on each thumb?
explanation: Iguanodon had a large spike on each thumb. It was a plant-eating dinosaur with hands that were very different from ours.
hint: Think about a feature on a dinosaur’s hand.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: How many legs did Tyrannosaurus rex walk on?
explanation: Tyrannosaurus rex walked on its two powerful back legs. Its arms were much smaller than its legs.
hint: Compare its arms with its back legs.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory

text: Which food would suit a plant-eating Triceratops?
explanation: Triceratops was a herbivore. Its beak and teeth helped it eat plants, even though it had impressive horns.
hint: Horns do not tell us what an animal eats.
source: Natural History Museum, London — Dino Directory
